question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC)?

options.A: To reduce maternal illness and death from abortion complications
options.B: To provide permanent sterilization to all female patients
options.C: To investigate the legal circumstances of a pregnancy loss
options.D: To promote mandatory reporting of all spontaneous miscarriages

explanation: Great job! PAC is all about saving lives and treating any physical or emotional issues after a pregnancy loss so the patient can recover safely.

question: Why is post-abortion care viewed as a complete package rather than just a single medical procedure?

options.A: It must involve legal teams alongside medical doctors in every case
options.B: It requires multiple surgical operations over a span of several months
options.C: It combines emergency treatment, counseling, contraception, and health linkages
options.D: It is only performed in specialized tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Spot on! PAC covers more than just the immediate physical cleanup—it looks at the whole person by offering counseling, family planning, and follow-up support.

question: How many core elements make up the standard post-abortion care framework?
explanation: You got it! The standard PAC framework is built on five key elements that guide clinical care and community support.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the five core elements of post-abortion care?
explanation: Correct! PAC is strictly about health, safety, and support—not punitive legal investigations. Our job as nurses is medical care.

question: What is the preferred method for first-trimester uterine evacuation in post-abortion care?
explanation: Well done! Manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) is widely preferred because it is safe, highly effective, and much gentler than older methods.

question: A patient comes in with an incomplete abortion showing fever, lower belly pain, and foul-smelling discharge. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.A: Send the patient home with instructions to return next week
options.B: Administer high-dose fertility drugs to stimulate ovulation
options.C: Prepare for broad-spectrum antibiotics and report signs of infection
options.D: Withhold all fluids to prevent vomiting during the assessment

explanation: Spot on! Fever and foul discharge are classic warning signs of a septic abortion. Immediate antibiotics and medical stabilization are lifesavers here.

question: Why are active listening and a non-judgmental attitude so important during post-abortion counseling?

options.A: It prevents patients from ever experiencing normal grief
options.B: It replaces the need for any physical medical treatments
options.C: It helps patients process diverse emotional reactions safely
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will choose permanent sterilization

explanation: You got it! Everyone reacts differently emotionally, and offering a safe, open space lets patients express themselves without fear of being judged.

question: What is a common emotional response a patient might experience after an abortion?

options.A: An immediate desire to write a public memoir about the event
options.B: Complete emotional numbness that lasts for an entire lifetime
options.C: A wide range of feelings including relief, grief, or anxiety
options.D: Permanent clinical detachment from all family members

explanation: Exactly! Feelings after pregnancy loss are deeply personal and can span anywhere from sadness and anxiety to relief.

question: How soon can a person start ovulating again after experiencing an abortion?

options.B: Only after a full year passes

explanation: Correct! Fertility can return surprisingly fast—sometimes in just two weeks—which is why talking about contraception early is so crucial.

question: When is the best time to discuss family planning options with a patient receiving post-abortion care?

options.A: Before the patient is discharged from the clinical setting
options.B: Only after the patient experiences a second unplanned pregnancy
options.C: Refer them to a distant pharmacy without discussing options
options.D: Wait until six months have passed to avoid overwhelming them

explanation: Spot on! Bringing up family planning before discharge ensures the patient is protected against a quick repeat pregnancy while they are still connected to care.

question: Why are community referrals and health linkages important in post-abortion care?

options.A: They replace the need for emergency treatment during complications
options.B: They ensure that the patient never has to visit a hospital again
options.C: They support long-term wellness and prevent future reproductive health issues
options.D: They are only used to track legal infractions in the community

explanation: Well done! Community linkages connect patients to ongoing check-ups, STI care, and other vital primary health resources.

question: Which group of people often acts as a bridge between local communities and clinical PAC facilities?
explanation: Correct! Community health workers play a wonderful role in guiding patients to local support networks and follow-up care.

question: How does social stigma directly affect patients who need post-abortion care?

options.A: It guarantees faster recovery times inside the emergency ward
options.B: It encourages patients to attend more routine health checkups
options.C: It delays patients from seeking timely and life-saving medical attention
options.D: It improves the emotional rapport between nurses and patients

explanation: Spot on! Fear of being judged or mistreated often forces patients to hide their symptoms, delaying the urgent care they need.

question: What is a core professional duty of a nurse caring for a PAC patient?

options.A: Providing unbiased, confidential, and compassionate medical care
options.B: Reporting the patient to local law enforcement authorities
options.C: Sharing clinical details publicly to educate the community
options.D: Refusing treatment if personal beliefs conflict with the diagnosis

explanation: You nailed it! As nurses, we are ethically bound to treat every patient with dignity, total confidentiality, and professional kindness.
